html:
Morocco is the kingdom in the far north-west of Africa, facing both the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. The map shows it from 1300 to 2010, and for all that time it was ruled by Moroccan dynasties, except for 44 years as a French and Spanish protectorate.

The state traces its start to the Idrisid dynasty in 788. Its peak came under the Berber Almoravids and Almohads in the 1000s and 1100s, who ruled Spain's south as well. The dynasties in the years on the map:

  • Marinids (1244 to 1465), Zenata Berbers who built colleges in Fez. The traveller Ibn Battuta set out from Tangier in their time.
  • Wattasids (1472 to 1554), who lost coastal towns to Portugal.
  • Saadis (1549 to 1659). They crushed a Portuguese invasion at the Battle of the Three Kings in 1578, where King Sebastian of Portugal died. Ahmad al-Mansur then sent an army across the Sahara that broke the Songhai at Tondibi in 1591.
  • Alaouites (from the 1660s), who still reign.

Morocco was the one North African country the Ottomans never ruled. In 1912 France and Spain divided it into protectorates. It regained independence in 1956. King Hassan II ruled from 1961 to 1999, and in 1975 his Green March pushed Moroccan control into Western Sahara, a claim still disputed.
